name: Heyflow

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial with no card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual discount is advertised as up to 31% on the plan table but up to 51% in the FAQ, and exact annual tier prices are not exposed; annual commitments are billed upfront unless invoicing terms are negotiated
pricing.hiddenCosts: Lead-generation overages/add-ons: responses from €0.15 ($0.17) each, extra funnel €8 ($9.23), Design/Conversion/Insights/Advanced Integrations €40 ($46.16) each/month, Coding €90 ($103.86), Security €30 ($34.62), Success €100 ($115.40), and extra seat €35 ($40.39). E-commerce Prime overages are €10 ($11.54) per 1,000 visitors, €80 ($92.32) per 25,000 visitors, €100 ($115.40) per 10 extra funnels, and €35 ($40.39) per seat. VAT is extra.

verdictSummary: The visible interactive form flows loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Heyflow earns its keep through delivery, integrations, compliance, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a interactive form flows tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: SMTP or transactional email key in .env
whatYouLose: spam and abuse defense at scale
whyPeopleStillPay: Heyflow: Customers pay for dependable collection, spam control, notifications, integrations, and confidence that responses will not disappear.
ongoingBurden: Own storage, webhooks, email delivery, spam, file uploads, privacy requests, schema changes, and uptime.

priorArt.name: HeyForm
priorArt.desc: Open-source form builder and collection backend.

alternatives.name: Typebot
alternatives.desc: Conversational landing flows with branching, calculations, payments, and analytics; the licence is fair-source, not open-source

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose/manual deployment of builder and viewer
facts.engines: Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, ElevenLabs and Dify through built-in integration blocks; API credentials are supplied by the user
facts.dataFormat: Hosted bots and results live in Typebot Cloud; self-hosted data lives in PostgreSQL and uploaded files in S3-compatible object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Typebot can branch, calculate, take payments, and track results, but it is less capable as a freely designed landing page and offers weaker out-of-the-box funnel analytics than Heyflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage, two web apps, DNS/TLS and mail/auth configuration; the licence is Fair Source rather than OSI open source.

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.desc: Multi-page forms, calculations, conditional logic, and result pages are free; removing the branding is not

facts.engines: Tally AI is available, but its underlying model provider is not publicly documented
facts.dataFormat: Forms and responses live in Tally's EU-hosted cloud; responses can be downloaded as CSV or synchronized to Google Sheets or Notion.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tally supports multi-page logic and calculations for free, but custom domains, branding removal, and detailed drop-off analytics are paid and its layout freedom is narrower than Heyflow's.

alternatives.name: Forminator
alternatives.desc: Forms, quizzes, calculators, and payments for free, provided the landing page lives in WordPress

facts.install: Install and activate the Forminator plugin from WordPress Admin
facts.dataFormat: Forms and submissions are stored in the site's WordPress database; uploaded files are stored in WordPress uploads, and submissions can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Forminator provides forms, quizzes, calculations, and payments, but it only lives inside WordPress and lacks Heyflow's standalone landing-flow polish and analytics.
facts.setupBlocker: It only runs inside an existing WordPress site, so hosting, WordPress maintenance and mail delivery must already be solved.

rejectedAlternatives.name: HeyForm
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Polished multi-step forms, but no calculator or formula-driven result engine

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Heyflow is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Heyflow, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a interactive form flows tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large integration and template catalog; compliance controls and guaranteed delivery; enterprise workflow logic.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
